newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities sells retail unit to Kingfisher.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities sells retail unit to Kingfisher.

text.p: United Utilities on Tuesday announced the sale of its NORWEB Retail business for 29 million pounds ($48 million) to retailer Kingfisher, which said hundreds of jobs will go.
"I cannot give you an exact figure, but it will be hundreds of people. That's for sure," a Kingfisher spokesman said.
NORWEB Retail, which operates 138 stores selling electrical goods mainly in the northeast of England, has annual sales of around 280 million pounds and employs about 2,800 people.
Kingfisher's Comet unit buys the 81 out-of-town stores after United Utilies already decided to close 57 high street shops. It also had plans to shut all the out-of-town stores.
"We will keep some of the out-of-town stores. But we will have to review the whole situation before we can decide which to keep and which to let go," the Kingfisher spokesman said.
Kingfisher's Comet wil definitely close NORWEB Retail's headquarters in Bolton and the Worsley distribution centre.

"Having considered all the options available, I am convinced that Kingfisher's offer represents the best value for United Utilities and the best alternative for NORWEB Retail and its employees," said Brian Staples, United Utilities' chief executive.
The NORWEB Retail disposal makes United Utilities the latest utility to sell off its electrical retail unit amid cut-throat competition in the high street.
United Utilities will retain reinsurance company Carefree Insurance Limited, which provides extended warranty and credit protection insurance for NORWEB Retail.
NORWEB Retail's loan portfolio was sold earlier to Lombard Tricity Finance Limited. The total amount raised so far from the sale of the NORWEB Retail division is 142 million pounds. ($1=.6050 Pound)
